paragraphs.source_en: Sakuma Shôzan (1811–64), who wrote earlier of the Opium War in China, emerged as another critic of moral decline in the Tokugawa years, but embraced a more practical approach. His slogan, ‘eastern ethics as base, Western technology as means’, straddled the two ideological camps. He believed that Japan needed to restore the emperor to power to stop Japan’s moral decline, while also embracing Western technology to defend itself. The urgency of the situation in China necessitated a practical approach, and ‘expelling the barbarians’, no matter how compelling, was impossible until Japan adopted the requisite military technology to do so.
